Friends. A sitcom that aired on NBC from nineteen ninety-four to two thousand four, following six twentysomethings—Rachel, Monica, Phoebe, Ross, Chandler, and Joey—navigating careers, relationships, and friendship in New York City. The show centered emotional weight on the ensemble bond itself; the will-they-won't-they romantic plots were secondary to the core appeal of watching friends support, betray, and reunite with each other.

The cast starred Jennifer Aniston as Rachel Green, Courteney Cox as Monica Geller, Lisa Kudrow as Phoebe Buffay, David Schwimmer as Ross Geller, Matthew Perry as Chandler Bing, and Matt LeBlanc as Joey Tribbiani. The show was set primarily in the characters' apartments and at Central Perk, a coffeehouse where the group gathered; the setting became almost a character itself. The central relationship was Ross and Rachel's on-and-off romance, a will-they-won't-they plotline stretched across all ten seasons.

Jennifer Aniston's "Rachel" haircut became a cultural phenomenon; women requested the hairstyle so frequently that it became iconic of the nineteen-nineties. Friends won fifty-nine Emmy nominations and received praise for its inclusive casting and portrayal of diverse sexualities. Episodes followed a classic sitcom structure: problem in the first act, complications in the second, resolution in the third.

Friends became a global phenomenon that defined nineteen-nineties television, influenced fashion and hairstyles, and established the friend group as the primary social unit in popular culture, challenging the family-centered sitcom of earlier decades.
